thread:
Sam: Heads up — I saw a perf regression on the FP8 canary after the latest calibration change. Throughput down ~12% on 8k sequences when KV hits are frequent.
Vika: ugh. which calibration change? the layerwise clipping tweak?
Sam: yeah, the per-channel clip shift we rolled yesterday. Microbench shows slower matmul kernel selection for mixed-precision layers.
Jordan: can you paste the profile? short snippet is fine.
Sam: pasted below — from local repro with batch=32, seq=8192, model=redwood/s1-7b-fp8-canary
Sam: ```
Perf summary:
  total_tokens: 2.6M
  avg_latency_token: 28.3ms -> 31.7ms (+12%)
  kernel_switches: 234 -> 612 (+161%)
  kv_lookup_rate: 72%
  hot_layers: [2,5,10,33,34]
```
Vika: kernel_switches jumping is the red flag — suggests selector couldn't pick an efficient int8/fp8 path and fell back to mixed or slower fp32 kernels.
Matt: is it specifically the embedding/lm_head path? those are excluded from quant typically.
Sam: embedding and lm_head are excluded in config, but the selector's per-layer sensitivity map changed so it started marking mid-layer attention heads as "sensitive" -> forcing safer kernel that doesn't use fused KV cache path. That breaks the hot-path for streaming KV.
Jordan: ah that would explain lowered KV hit efficiency. If the kernel can't use the hardware-friendly KV packing layout, we lose a lot.
Vika: do we have a diff of sensitivity thresholds? maybe the new calibration made more layers exceed the error budget.
Sam: I compared old vs new SensMap quickly:
Sam: ```
layer  old_err   new_err   sensitive?
2      0.0041   0.0056    yes
5      0.0038   0.0050    yes
10     0.0022   0.0024    no
33     0.0079   0.0095    yes
34     0.0071   0.0080    yes
```
Jordan: thresholds are still 0.005 by default right? looks like a few crossed the line.
Matt: crossed layers 2/5/33/34 are early & late-attention — heavy KV reuse. Losing fast KV kernel there is very costly.
Vika: quick mitigation: we could pin those layers to legacy fp8 kernel or explicitly exclude them from the sensitivity map until we tune calibration.
Sam: I tried a local canary with explicit per-layer override -> pinned layers to fp8-fused-kv and throughput recovered to +2% vs baseline.
Sam: ```
canary config snippet:
  quant_overrides:
    layers: [2,5,33,34]
    mode: force_fp8_fused_kv
```
Jordan: good proof. But we should root cause why calibration moved these errors up. Could be quant scale recomputation using per-channel moments with batchnorm-ish instability from small calibration set.
Vika: calibration used 200 random sequences from prod sampling window. Maybe not representative for these sequence lengths and prefix distributions.
Matt: also batching heuristics changed in the runtime last week (dynamic packer update) — different micro-batches could change activation distributions during calibration runs.
Sam: right — I ran a controlled calibration using long-sequence traces and the sensitivity metrics returned to previous values. So two interacting changes: calibration dataset + packer microbatching.
Jordan: TL;DR: calibration + packer change -> sensitivity map shifted -> kernel selector chooses slower kernels -> KV path degraded -> throughput drop.
Vika: action items: 1) revert calibration tweak or restrict it behind config flag, 2) add per-layer override in rollout for canary, 3) enhance perf tests to include high KV-hit long-seq scenarios.
Matt: + add a gating perf test that measures kernel_switch rate and KV packing efficiency in CI. We had token-latency checks but not kernel_switch counts.
Sam: already instrumented kernel_switch metric in perf-bot, added to the regression alert. perf-bot — can you post the failing canary link?
perf-bot: Canary run 1872549001 status: degraded. Metrics: 
- throughput: 188k tok/min (expected 212k)
- avg_token_latency: 31.7ms (expected 28.4ms)
- kernel_switch_rate: 2.6x baseline
- kv_packed_rate: 68% (baseline 91%)
deploy-bot: Canary 1872549001 -> paused by perf alert at 1872549800.
Jordan: for longer term: we should make sensitivity map calibration aware of KV-impact — i.e., factor in a KV-penalty when deciding sensitive vs tolerant. Currently it's purely quant-error-driven.
Vika: yes, a weighted decision: quant_error + alpha * (kv_hotness). Could avoid marking KV-hot layers as sensitive for tiny error increases.
Matt: propose alpha=0.7 initial, and we can sweep on canary. Also expose per-layer visualization in console so PMs can see which layers flip between calibrations.
Sam: I'll open a small RFC: "sensitivity-map: kv-aware scoring + canary overrides" and include the perf traces. Will also attach the quick revert patch to disable new calibration by default.
Vika: +1. Can we push the per-layer override to the canary rollout today to mitigate customer impact?
Sam: yes, I made the patch and will deploy a targeted canary to affected accounts. Pushing now.
deploy-bot: Patch queued: r/1234 by Sam -> starting canary on 4 hosts.
Jordan: thanks. After canary stabilizes let's run the kernel-level microbench (single layer hotpath) for layers 2/5/33/34 to validate numerical fidelity too.
Sam: will do. Also adding a small eval to confirm no quality regression after forcing fused-kv fp8.
Vika: great. keep this thread updated with canary numbers. :thumbsup:
Sam: will post an update in ~30m with canary metrics.
Sam: update (30m): canary throughput back to 211k tok/min, kv_packed_rate 90%, kernel_switch_rate back near baseline. Rolling the patch to remaining hosts gradually.
Jordan: nice. followup: please add CI perf test for long-seq KV heavy workload and a check that sensitivity flips are under a small delta unless calibration dataset changes.
Sam: noted, will add to eng-runtime perf-suite ticket.
